system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**MEMORANDUM**

**TO:** Amelia Frost & Wattlebridge Holdings Deal Team  
**FROM:** Legal Counsel (Wattlebridge Holdings Deal Team)  
**DATE:** 23 September 2026  
**SUBJECT:** Project Kestrel — Review of Seller’s Draft SPA, Update Positions, and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

---

### EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

We have critically reviewed the Seller’s (Harbourglass Ventures) draft SPA positions, Seller Update, and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003) against the **Wattlebridge Holdings Buyer Negotiation Playbook**. 

The Seller’s package represents an aggressive attempt to curtail Buyer protections, sweep core risks into restricted general caps, shift pre-completion liabilities onto the Buyer, and rely on broad deemed disclosures. 

Below is our detailed critique of where the Seller's draft departs from our playbook, the legal and commercial reasoning for pushing back, and our clear action items/recommendations for the upcoming mark-up.

---

### DETAILED ANALYSIS & PLAYBOOK COMPARISON

#### 1. General Warranty Cap & Claim Period (Clauses 12.1 & 12.3)
* **Seller Draft:** General warranty liability capped at 20% of the Purchase Price (AUD 4,800,000) with an 18-month claims limitation period.
* **Playbook Mandate:** 
  * General warranty cap starting position: **25% of Purchase Price (AUD 6,000,000)**.
  * General claims period starting position: **24 months post-Completion**.
  * *Note:* A 20% cap (AUD 4.8m) and an 18-month period are strictly fallback positions usable **only** with prior written authorization from Buyer Principal Amelia Frost specifically identifying the draft. No such approval has been granted.
* **Pushback & Legal Rationale:** Reject the 20% cap and 18-month timeframe. Revert Clause 12.1 to 25% (AUD 6,000,000) and Clause 12.3 to 24 months. We require two full audit cycles (24 months) to uncover operational, financial, or compliance breaches.

#### 2. Thresholds: De Minimis and Basket Structure (Clause 12.2)
* **Seller Draft:** De minimis threshold of AUD 25,000; aggregate basket of AUD 250,000; recoverable on an "excess-only" (deductible) basis.
* **Playbook Mandate:** De minimis of **AUD 5,000**; aggregate basket of **AUD 50,000**; recoverable on a **first-dollar tipping basis** (Seller liable for all losses from dollar one once the basket is reached).
* **Pushback & Legal Rationale:** The Seller’s proposed thresholds are unreasonably high for an AUD 24M deal, effectively insulating the Seller from substantial aggregate losses. Furthermore, an "excess-only" deductible shifts initial risk to Wattlebridge. We must insist on AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 aggregate basket, and first-dollar recovery.

#### 3. Fundamental & Title Warranties Regime (Clause 12.3 / 13 & Disclosures)
* **Seller Draft:** Capacity and Title warranties are folded into the general warranty regime, subject to the same 20% cap, 18-month time limit, general basket, and knowledge bars for "administrative simplicity." The Seller relies solely on internal share register DD-012 for title proof.
* **Playbook Mandate:** Fundamental and Title claims must sit in a standalone regime: **100% Purchase Price cap**, minimum **6-year limitation period**, completely carved out from the general basket, de minimis, and knowledge exclusions. Independent proof of title/encumbrances is required.
* **Pushback & Legal Rationale:** Ownership of 100% of Paperbark Analytics is the foundation of the transaction. A breach of title or authority goes to the core of the deal value and cannot be capped at 20% or cut off after 18 months. An internal share register (DD-012) is self-serving and insufficient. We must demand independent title evidence, full representations against encumbrances, and a dedicated fundamental warranty regime.

#### 4. Fraud, Wilful Concealment & Deliberate Misconduct Carve-Out (Clauses 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)
* **Seller Draft:** Blanket limitation, exclusive remedies, and non-reliance provisions applying to "all Claims of any nature" without exception.
* **Playbook Mandate:** Fraud, wilful concealment, and deliberate misconduct **must be expressly carved out** of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy clauses, and non-reliance provisions to the maximum extent legally enforceable.
* **Pushback & Legal Rationale:** It is commercially unacceptable and legally unconscionable to limit liability or waive remedies for intentional fraud or wilful concealment. Re-insert an explicit, non-negotiable carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment, and deliberate misconduct across all limitation and boilerplate provisions.

#### 5. Disclosure Framework (Schedule 7 & Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)
* **Seller Draft:** Broad general disclosure of the entire electronic data room (DD-002 to DD-012), statutory registers, and publicly searchable records.
* **Playbook Mandate:** Reject whole-data-room, public-register, or prudent-search deemed disclosures. Require specific, fair disclosure (fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the risk).
* **Pushback & Legal Rationale:** A blanket data dump shifts the due diligence burden entirely onto the Buyer and neutralizes warranty protection. We must strike general data room and public record disclosures from Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter sections 1.1/1.2, insisting on specific, qualified disclosures.

#### 6. Buyer Knowledge Qualifier (Clause 8.3)
* **Seller Draft:** Buyer cannot bring any claim regarding matters of which Buyer or its advisers had actual or constructible knowledge (including anything discoverable from public records or the data room).
* **Playbook Mandate:** Delete blanket Buyer knowledge exclusions. Any knowledge qualification must be strictly anchored to named Seller knowledge individuals after due enquiry, and must **never** excuse Title, Capacity, Fraud, or Specific Indemnities.
* **Pushback & Legal Rationale:** Clause 8.3 undermines the purpose of contractual warranties. Knowledge of an issue by a Buyer's advisor does not mean the Buyer accepted the risk or priced it into the deal. Delete Clause 8.3; align any Seller-knowledge qualifiers strictly to designated Seller executives following reasonable enquiry.

#### 7. Material Customer Consents — Bluefen (Clauses 3 / 6.3 & Disclosure 2)
* **Seller Draft:** Reasonable endeavours obligation only; treats Bluefen change-of-control consent as satisfied upon delivery of counterparty consent (ignoring consent conditions).
* **Playbook Mandate:** Bluefen (~30% FY26 revenue / ~AUD 3.6m) requires **effective consent AND verified evidence** that all underlying conditions (clause 11.3) are satisfied prior to Completion. Reasonable endeavours alone is unacceptable.
* **Pushback & Legal Rationale:** Receiving a conditional consent letter where conditions are unmet leaves Wattlebridge exposed to immediate termination or breach post-closing. Obtaining effective consent and satisfying Clause 11.3 conditions must be a mandatory Condition Precedent (CP) to Completion.

#### 8. Debt & Security Discharge — Riverlark Bank (Clauses 2 / 7 & Disclosure 3)
* **Seller Draft:** AUD 3.2M outstanding facility to be addressed post-Completion by a post-closing release.
* **Playbook Mandate:** Transaction is agreed on a **debt-free / cash-free basis**. Requires direct payout from Completion funds and effective, simultaneous security releases. Post-completion release requires irrevocable undertakings and Amelia Frost's express written approval.
* **Pushback & Legal Rationale:** Leaving an AUD 3.2M facility and security interest active post-closing breaches the debt-free baseline and leaves target assets encumbered. Payout letters, full bank discharge, and PPSR security releases must be delivered at Completion directly via the funds flow.

#### 9. Employee Closing Bonuses & Funds Flow (Disclosure 5 & Funds Flow)
* **Seller Draft:** AUD 
=== END ADVICE ===
